subject: Geography
central_question: How is water circulated through the hydrological cycle, and how are ocean-floor relief, temperature and salinity organised across the world’s oceans?
in_scope_units: Hydrological cycle and planetary water distribution
Horizontal and vertical temperature distribution and thermocline
Horizontal and vertical salinity distribution and halocline
NCERT exercises and atlas project work
banned_topics: Detailed waves, tides and current mechanics from Chapter 13
Detailed atmospheric humidity and rainfall from Chapter 10
Detailed plate-tectonic theory beyond the stated ocean-floor features

known_pitfalls.claim: The hydrological cycle permanently consumes water.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter calls water a cyclic resource used and reused through continuous exchange.

known_pitfalls.claim: The continental shelf is the steep transition into the deep ocean.
known_pitfalls.correction: The shelf is shallow and gentle; the continental slope is the steep descent beyond the shelf break.

known_pitfalls.claim: Ocean temperature decreases uniformly with depth.
known_pitfalls.correction: The rate is not uniform; the thermocline is the zone of rapid decrease.
Precipitation, river inflow, freezing and thawing, wind and currents also matter.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 3(i): interrelate the hydrological cycle
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1, 2 and 3 and Project Work using an atlas to map ocean-floor relief and ridges.
